---
title: "How school absence changes"
subtitle: "Following every secondary school in England from 2016/17 to 2025/26: what stays with a school, what moves, and what happens when its intake, status or trust changes."
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
A <- readRDS(here::here("data", "absence_change.rds"))
OUT <- A$outcomes
OUT_SHORT <- c(overall = "Overall", illness = "Illness", appointments = "Medical\nappointments",
               auth_other = "Other\nauthorised", unauth = "Unauthorised", persistent = "Persistent\n(10%+)",
               severe = "Severe\n(50%+)")
OUT_LOW <- c(overall = "overall absence", illness = "illness absence", appointments = "medical appointments",
             auth_other = "other authorised absence", unauth = "unauthorised absence",
             persistent = "persistent absence", severe = "severe absence")
tr  <- function(tp, col) A$trend[[col]][A$trend$tp == tp]
vd  <- function(o, lev) 100 * A$var_dec$share[A$var_dec$outcome == o & A$var_dec$level == lev]
cr  <- function(o, a, b) A$cors$r[A$cors$outcome == o & A$cors$a == a & A$cors$b == b]
sa  <- function(o, col) A$shift$all[[col]][A$shift$all$outcome == o]
sq  <- function(o, q, col) A$shift$by_fsm[[col]][A$shift$by_fsm$outcome == o & A$shift$by_fsm$fsm_q == q]
ktop <- function(o, col) A$shift$keep_top[[col]][A$shift$keep_top$outcome == o]
wbv <- function(o, m, t, col = "pct") A$wb[[col]][A$wb$outcome == o & A$wb$model == m & A$wb$term == t]
wr2 <- function(o) 100 * A$wb$r2_within[A$wb$outcome == o & A$wb$model == "Within"][1]
xm  <- function(t, col) A$x_move[[col]][A$x_move$term == t]
it  <- function(tp, col) A$intake_trend[[col]][A$intake_trend$tp == tp]
ATT <- bind_rows(lapply(A$es, `[[`, "att")) |>
  mutate(pct = pct(est), lo = pct(est - 1.96 * se), hi = pct(est + 1.96 * se))
att <- function(st, o, col = "pct") ATT[[col]][ATT$study == st & ATT$outcome == o]
EV <- bind_rows(lapply(A$es[c("conversion", "trust")], `[[`, "event")) |>
  mutate(pct = pct(est), lo = pct(est - 1.96 * se), hi = pct(est + 1.96 * se))
evp <- function(st, o, r) EV$pct[EV$study == st & EV$outcome == o & EV$rel == r]
nev <- function(k) sum(A$es[[k]]$n$n[A$es[[k]]$n$kind != "Never"])
comp <- function(st, m, col = "est") A$es_comp[[col]][A$es_comp$study == st & A$es_comp$measure == m]
X_LAB <- c(fsm = "Free school meals", sen_sup = "SEN support", ehcp = "EHC plans", eal = "EAL",
           girls = "Girls", lsize = "Size")
UNIT_LAB <- c(fsm = "5 points more pupils on FSM", sen_sup = "5 points more on SEN support",
              ehcp = "1 point more with EHC plans", eal = "5 points more with EAL",
              girls = "10 points more girls", lsize = "10% more pupils")
P <- A$panel
yrs <- function(x) paste0(substr(x, 1, 4), "/", substr(x, 5, 6))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Work in progress

This page continues the [absence analysis](absence_causes.qmd). That page
compares different schools in one year. This one follows the same schools
over ten years. Every figure comes from published school-level data, so
every result is about schools, not pupils.
:::

## Why follow schools over time

Comparing schools in one year mixes up two things: what a school's pupils
and community bring, and what the school does. Following the *same* school
over time holds constant everything about it that does not change: its
neighbourhood, its buildings, its reputation, most of its intake. What is
left is change. So this page asks:

1. How much of a school's absence is lasting, and how much moves from
   year to year?
2. Do schools keep their place?
3. Who rose most between before the pandemic and now?
4. When a school's own intake changes, does its absence change with it?
5. What happens to absence when a school becomes an academy, or moves to a
   new trust?

## The data {#sec-data}

- **Absence.** DfE's school-level absence for the autumn and spring terms,
  2016/17 to 2025/26. It is the one file that covers every year on the same
  basis, including 2025/26, whose full-year figures are not published
  until 2027. 2019/20 was not collected. 2020/21 is shown in the trend but left
  out of every model: in a year of lockdowns, pupils told to stay home were
  not counted as absent.
- **Schools.** Every state-funded secondary school: `r format(P$school_years, big.mark = ",")`
  school-years, `r format(P$schools, big.mark = ",")` schools. A school
  that becomes an academy, or moves trust, gets a new URN. The
  `r format(P$urns, big.mark = ",")` URNs are joined into schools with
  GIAS's one-to-one predecessor and successor links. Mergers,
  amalgamations and splits end a school's record.
- **Intake.** The January school census for 2018/19 and 2021/22 to
  2024/25 (the performance tables' census files) and 2025/26 (the January
  2026 school census and SEN files). Earlier years are no longer published
  in the same form.

## Ten years of absence {#sec-trend}

```{r}
#| label: fig-index
#| fig-cap: "Absence in England's state-funded secondary schools, autumn and spring terms, indexed to 2018/19 = 100 (sessions-weighted for the reasons; % of pupils for persistent and severe). 2019/20 was not collected; 2020/21 (shaded) was a year of partial closure."
#| fig-height: 4.6
ix <- A$trend |>
  transmute(tp, Overall = overall, Illness, `Other authorised`,
            Unauthorised = `Unauthorised holiday` + `Other unauthorised`,
            `Persistent (10%+)` = persistent, `Severe (50%+)` = severe) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-tp, names_to = "measure", values_to = "v") |>
  group_by(measure) |> mutate(ix = 100 * v / v[tp == 201819L]) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(x = tp %/% 100)
ix <- bind_rows(ix, tibble(x = 2019L, measure = unique(ix$measure))) |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, c("Severe (50%+)", "Other authorised", "Unauthorised",
                                     "Persistent (10%+)", "Overall", "Illness")))
# spread the end labels so they do not collide
lab <- ix |> filter(x == 2025) |> arrange(ix) |> mutate(y = ix)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(lab))[-1]) lab$y[i] <- max(lab$y[i], lab$y[i - 1] + 11)
ggplot(ix, aes(x, ix, colour = measure)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2019.5, xmax = 2020.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = PPURPLE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = LIGHT) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) + geom_point(size = 1.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(data = lab, aes(y = y, label = paste0(measure, "  ", round(ix))),
            hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.15, size = 3.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(DPURPLE, BPURPLE, BLUE, MPURPLE, INK, GREY), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2016:2025, labels = function(x) paste0(x, "/", substr(x + 1, 3, 4)),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.3))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "2018/19 = 100") + theme_note()
```

Absence across the autumn and spring terms rose from
`r pp(tr(201819L, "overall"))`% of sessions in 2018/19 to
`r pp(tr(202223L, "overall"))`% in 2022/23. It has eased only to
`r pp(tr(202526L, "overall"))`% in 2025/26. Illness has fallen most of the
way back. Unauthorised and other authorised absence have not.
Severe absence, pupils missing half their schooling or more, has risen
from `r pp(tr(201819L, "severe"))`% of pupils to
`r pp(tr(202526L, "severe"))`%, and is still near its peak.

## What stays with a school and what moves {#sec-variance}

```{r}
#| label: fig-variance
#| fig-cap: "Where the variation in each kind of absence lies, once the national year-to-year swing is taken out: multilevel models of log absence with year effects and region, local authority and school random effects, 2016/17 to 2025/26 without 2020/21. 'Year to year' is a school's movement around its own lasting level."
#| fig-height: 3.8
LEV_COL <- c("Region" = GREY, "Local authority" = BLUE, "School (lasting)" = DPURPLE, "Year to year" = LPURPLE)
vdf <- A$var_dec |>
  mutate(level = factor(level, rev(names(LEV_COL))), out = factor(OUT_SHORT[outcome], rev(OUT_SHORT)))
ggplot(vdf, aes(100 * share, out, fill = level)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(share >= 0.08, round(100 * share), "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            colour = ifelse(vdf$level %in% c("School (lasting)", "Local authority", "Region"), "white", INK), size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LEV_COL, breaks = names(LEV_COL), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "% of the variation, after national year effects", y = NULL) + theme_note() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

- **Most absence is lasting.** Once the national swing from year to year
  is taken out, `r round(vd("overall", "School (lasting)"))`% of the
  variation in overall absence, `r round(vd("unauth", "School (lasting)"))`%
  of unauthorised and `r round(vd("persistent", "School (lasting)"))`% of
  persistent absence is a school's lasting level. Its region and local
  authority account for about a tenth; the rest is movement from year to
  year.
- **Illness moves more, and is more about place.** Only
  `r round(vd("illness", "School (lasting)"))`% of the variation in illness
  is lasting to a school, `r round(vd("illness", "Year to year"))`% moves
  from year to year, and `r round(vd("illness", "Local authority"))`% is the
  local authority. That fits the cross-section, where illness was the kind
  of absence most tied to place.
- **The national swing is large.** Year alone accounts for
  `r round(100 * A$year_share[["overall"]])`% of all the variation in
  overall absence over the period, and `r round(100 * A$year_share[["severe"]])`%
  of severe. Any one school's change from last year is mostly the country's
  change.

## Do schools keep their place? {#sec-stability}

```{r}
#| label: fig-cors
#| fig-cap: "Correlation between years of each school's absence relative to England that year (log scale), for the schools present in both years. 2020/21 is included here for completeness."
#| fig-height: 7.2
#| fig-width: 9
cc <- A$cors |> filter(outcome %in% c("overall", "unauth", "illness", "severe"), a > b) |>
  mutate(out = factor(sub("\n", " ", OUT_SHORT[outcome]), sub("\n", " ", OUT_SHORT)), A_ = yrs(a), B_ = yrs(b))
ggplot(cc, aes(B_, A_, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r), colour = r > 0.7), size = 2.9) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#f7f4fb", LPURPLE, MPURPLE, BPURPLE, DPURPLE), limits = c(0.2, 1),
                       oob = scales::squish, name = "Correlation") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = INK), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ out, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_note(11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"))
```

From one year to the next, schools barely move: the correlation of overall
absence between 2024/25 and 2025/26 is `r pp(cr("overall", 202526L, 202425L), 2)`.
Over longer stretches they do. Between 2018/19, before the pandemic, and
2025/26 the correlation is `r pp(cr("overall", 202526L, 201819L), 2)` for
overall absence, `r pp(cr("unauth", 202526L, 201819L), 2)` for
unauthorised and only `r pp(cr("illness", 202526L, 201819L), 2)` for
illness.

Put another way, of the fifth of schools with the highest unauthorised
absence before the pandemic (2016/17 to 2018/19),
`r round(100 * ktop("unauth", "stay"))`% are still in the top fifth now
(2023/24 to 2025/26). For overall absence it is
`r round(100 * ktop("overall", "stay"))`%. If nothing changed, it would be
20%. If nothing moved, 100%. A school's place is sticky, but it is not
fixed: more than a third of the schools with the most absence before the
pandemic no longer have.

## Before the pandemic and now {#sec-shift}

```{r}
#| label: fig-shift
#| fig-cap: "Average absence before the pandemic (2016/17 to 2018/19, pale) and now (2023/24 to 2025/26, dark), by fifth of schools on free school meals in 2018/19. Labels: the rise as % of where each group started."
#| fig-height: 5.4
QL <- A$shift$base_q |> mutate(lab = paste0(c("Fewest", "2nd", "3rd", "4th", "Most"), "\n",
                                            round(lo), "–", round(hi), "%"))
sh <- A$shift$by_fsm |> filter(outcome %in% c("overall", "unauth", "persistent", "severe")) |>
  mutate(out = factor(sub("\n", " ", OUT_SHORT[outcome]), sub("\n", " ", OUT_SHORT)), q = factor(QL$lab[fsm_q], QL$lab))
ggplot(sh, aes(q)) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = q, y = pre, yend = post), colour = LIGHT, linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pre), colour = MPURPLE, size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(y = post), colour = DPURPLE, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(y = post, label = sprintf("+%.0f%%", pct)), vjust = -1, size = 3.1, colour = INK) +
  facet_wrap(~ out, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(x = "Schools by share of pupils on free school meals, 2018/19 (fifths)", y = "%") + theme_note(11)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-shift
#| tbl-cap: "Average school absence before the pandemic and now, schools with at least two years in each period."
A$shift$all |> mutate(o = factor(outcome, names(OUT))) |> arrange(o) |>
  transmute(`Kind of absence` = OUT[outcome], Schools = format(schools, big.mark = ","),
            `2016/17 to 2018/19` = pp(pre, 2), `2023/24 to 2025/26` = pp(post, 2),
            `Change (points)` = sgn(pp, 2), `Change (%)` = sgn(pct, 0)) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrr")
```

- **The rise was broadly proportional.** Schools with the fewest pupils on
  free school meals saw overall absence rise by
  `r round(sq("overall", 1, "pct"))`%. Schools with the most saw
  `r round(sq("overall", 5, "pct"))`%. In percentage points, the gap
  widened: `r pp(sq("overall", 1, "pp"))` points against
  `r pp(sq("overall", 5, "pp"))`.
- **Unauthorised absence doubled almost everywhere**, slightly less in
  the poorest schools in relative terms
  (`r sgn(sq("unauth", 5, "pct"), 0)`% against `r sgn(sq("unauth", 1, "pct"), 0)`%)
  but by far more in points.
- **Severe absence roughly tripled in every fifth**, from
  `r pp(sq("severe", 1, "pre"))`% of pupils to `r pp(sq("severe", 1, "post"))`%
  in the least disadvantaged schools and from `r pp(sq("severe", 5, "pre"))`%
  to `r pp(sq("severe", 5, "post"))`% in the most.
- **Illness rose least in the poorest schools**
  (`r sgn(sq("illness", 5, "pct"), 0)`% against `r sgn(sq("illness", 2, "pct"), 0)`%
  in the second fifth).

So the pandemic did not reorder schools so much as scale them up. A
school's absence now is best compared with where it was *relative to
England* before, not with its own pre-pandemic figure.

## When a school's own intake changes {#sec-within}

The cross-section shows that schools with more pupils on free school meals
or SEN support have more absence. That could be because of those pupils,
or because of everything else that goes with being that kind of school.
Following the same school as its intake changes separates the two. If a
school's absence moves with its own intake, the intake matters directly.
If not, the cross-school pattern is mostly about the kind of school and
community.

```{r}
#| label: fig-within
#| fig-cap: "Difference in absence (%) with a change in intake, between schools (pooled, with year effects; pale) and within the same school over time (school and year fixed effects; dark), 2018/19 and 2021/22 to 2025/26, with 95% intervals clustered by school."
#| fig-height: 6.2
wd <- A$wb |> filter(outcome %in% c("overall", "unauth", "persistent", "severe")) |>
  mutate(out = factor(sub("\n", " ", OUT_SHORT[outcome]), sub("\n", " ", OUT_SHORT)),
         lab = factor(UNIT_LAB[term], rev(UNIT_LAB)),
         model = factor(ifelse(model == "Within", "Within the same school", "Between schools"),
                        c("Between schools", "Within the same school")))
ggplot(wd, aes(pct, lab, colour = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = LIGHT) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ out, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Between schools" = MPURPLE, "Within the same school" = DPURPLE), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "% difference in absence", y = NULL) + theme_note(11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

- **Between schools, disadvantage goes with far more unauthorised
  absence than within one.** Across schools, five points more pupils on
  free school meals goes with `r sgn(wbv("unauth", "Between", "fsm"), 0)`%
  unauthorised absence. When one school's own share rises by as much, its
  unauthorised absence rises by `r sgn(wbv("unauth", "Within", "fsm"), 0)`%.
  Most of the cross-school gradient is about the kind of school and
  community, not the marginal pupil.
- **The same holds for SEN support**: `r sgn(wbv("unauth", "Between", "sen_sup"), 0)`%
  between schools, `r sgn(wbv("unauth", "Within", "sen_sup"), 0)`% within.
- **For overall absence the two are closer** (`r sgn(wbv("overall", "Between", "fsm"), 1)`%
  and `r sgn(wbv("overall", "Within", "fsm"), 1)`% for FSM), so a school
  taking more disadvantaged pupils should expect somewhat more absence.
- **Intake change explains little of how a school's absence moves.** The
  changes in intake account for `r pp(wr2("overall"))`% of the
  within-school variation in overall absence, `r pp(wr2("unauth"))`% of
  unauthorised and `r pp(wr2("persistent"))`% of persistent. Intake does
  not move much within a school (@tbl-move), and when absence moves, it is
  mostly something else.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-move
#| tbl-cap: "How much intake varies between schools and within a school over time (standard deviations, 2018/19 and 2021/22 to 2025/26)."
A$x_move |> transmute(Characteristic = A$x[term], `Between schools` = pp(between_sd, 2),
                      `Within a school over time` = pp(within_sd, 2)) |> kt(align = "lrr")
```

The share of pupils on free school meals almost doubled over the period
(`r pp(it(201819L, "fsm"))`% in 2018/19, `r pp(it(202526L, "fsm"))`% in
2025/26), much of it because pupils who became eligible under Universal
Credit kept their eligibility. The year effects take out the national rise,
but where it rose faster it may not mean more poverty. Leaving out
2025/26, whose intake comes from a different file, makes little difference
(see [the full results](#sec-full)).

## Becoming an academy, or changing trust {#sec-events}

Two kinds of change give a school a new URN, so they can be dated
precisely:

- **Becoming an academy.** `r nev("conversion")` maintained schools
  converted between 2017/18 and 2025/26 and can be followed either side,
  compared with schools that were maintained throughout and those that had
  yet to convert.
- **A change of trust.** `r nev("trust")` academies moved to a new trust,
  compared with academies that stayed put.

Each is an event study (Sun and Abraham's estimator, with school and year
effects): how absence moved, relative to similar schools that did not
change, in the years before and after. The years count only the years with
data, so the pandemic gap is one step.

```{r}
#| label: fig-events
#| fig-cap: "Absence before and after a school becomes an academy (top) or moves to a new trust (bottom), relative to the year before (0) and to schools that did not change, % with 95% intervals clustered by school. Event times with fewer than 25 schools are not shown."
#| fig-height: 6.4
ev <- EV |> filter(outcome %in% c("overall", "unauth", "persistent", "severe"), rel >= -5, rel <= 5,
                   is.na(schools) | schools >= 25) |>
  mutate(out = factor(sub("\n", " ", OUT_SHORT[outcome]), sub("\n", " ", OUT_SHORT)),
         study = factor(study, c("Becoming an academy", "A change of trust")))
ggplot(ev, aes(rel, pct)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -0.5, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = PPURPLE, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = LPURPLE, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(colour = DPURPLE, linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(colour = DPURPLE, size = 1.8) +
  facet_grid(study ~ out) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-5, 5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Years before (−) and after the change (years with data)", y = "% difference") +
  theme_note(10.5) + theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-events
#| tbl-cap: "Average difference in absence in the years after the change (% with 95% interval), and in the pupils."
ATT |> filter(study %in% c("Becoming an academy", "Converter academies only", "A change of trust")) |>
  mutate(o = factor(outcome, names(OUT)), s = factor(study, c("Becoming an academy", "Converter academies only", "A change of trust"))) |>
  arrange(s, o) |>
  transmute(s, Kind = OUT[outcome], v = sprintf("%+.1f%% (%+.1f to %+.1f)", pct, lo, hi)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = s, values_from = v) |>
  bind_rows(A$es_comp |>
    mutate(v = ifelse(grepl("log", measure), sprintf("%+.1f%% (%+.1f to %+.1f)", pct(est), pct(est - 1.96 * se), pct(est + 1.96 * se)),
                      sprintf("%+.1f (%+.1f to %+.1f)", est, est - 1.96 * se, est + 1.96 * se)),
           Kind = sub(" \\(log\\)", "", measure)) |>
    select(study, Kind, v) |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = study, values_from = v)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ coalesce(.x, "–"))) |>
  kt(align = "lrrr") |>
  kableExtra::pack_rows("Absence", 1, 6) |> kableExtra::pack_rows("Pupils", 7, 9)
```

**Becoming an academy makes no clear difference.** In the years after
conversion, overall absence was within `r pp(abs(att("Becoming an academy", "overall")))`%
of schools that stayed maintained (95% interval
`r sgn(att("Becoming an academy", "overall", "lo"), 1)`% to
`r sgn(att("Becoming an academy", "overall", "hi"), 1)`%). But the converting
schools were already on a different path: their absence was rising
relative to schools that stayed maintained in the years before, and that
rise stopped. So the honest reading is no visible effect of conversion
itself, among schools whose trajectory was already diverging.

**A change of trust is followed by lower absence.** In the years after a
move, unauthorised absence was `r round(-att("A change of trust", "unauth"))`%
lower and persistent absence `r round(-att("A change of trust", "persistent"))`%
lower, relative to academies that stayed with their trust. Overall absence
was `r round(-att("A change of trust", "overall"))`% lower. Three things to
weigh:

1. **The schools were getting worse first.** Absence rose in the two or
   three years before the move (persistent absence three years before was
   `r round(-evp("A change of trust", "persistent", -3))`% lower than in the
   year before), which is often why a school is moved. Some of the fall is
   recovery. But persistent and unauthorised absence fell well below where
   they had been three years before the move.
2. **The pupils did not get easier.** The share on free school meals rose
   by `r sgn(comp("A change of trust", "Free school meals (points)"), 1)`
   points relative to other academies, and the roll changed little.
3. **Recording may change too.** A new trust brings new attendance
   policies, and how sessions are coded is partly a school's choice. Other
   authorised absence also fell, so this is not just unauthorised absence
   being authorised instead.

## What it means {#sec-means}

::: {.callout-tip}
## For heads and governors

1. **Judge your absence against England's year, not your own last
   year.** The national swing is the largest single thing in any school's
   change from one year to the next.
2. **Compare with where you stood relative to England before the pandemic,
   not with your pre-pandemic figures.** Everyone's rose, and roughly in
   proportion.
3. **A school's absence is mostly lasting, but not fixed.** Two-thirds of
   the variation is a school's own level, and the same schools tend to stay
   high. More than a third of the highest-absence schools before the
   pandemic are no longer in the top fifth.
4. **A change in intake is rarely the reason absence moved.** Within a
   school, changes in its pupils explain only a few per cent of changes in
   absence.
5. **What happens in the school seems to matter.** A change of trust,
   which usually means new leadership and new attendance policies, is
   followed by lower unauthorised and persistent absence, even with more
   disadvantaged pupils. To see who has done it with an intake like yours,
   [Find a twin](twins.qmd).
:::

For policy, the same results say that the post-pandemic rise is a national
shift, not something concentrated in a few kinds of school, and that
structural change (becoming an academy) is not by itself a lever on
attendance. What a new trust does might be.

## What this cannot tell us {#sec-limits}

- **It is about schools, not pupils.** A school's absence can change
  because its pupils change, or because the same pupils attend differently.
  Published data cannot tell these apart.
- **Event studies are not experiments.** Schools are moved to a new trust
  for reasons, often falling standards. The comparison schools did not face
  the same pressures, and the pre-move rise shows it.
- **Recording practice varies.** Whether a session is coded as illness,
  authorised or unauthorised is partly a school's choice, and can change
  with a new head or trust.
- **The intake series is short and its FSM measure shifted.** Intake by
  year is available for six years, and eligibility under Universal Credit
  raised FSM shares in ways that do not all reflect more poverty.
- **Chains break.** A school that merges or splits starts a new record, so
  the most disrupted schools are under-represented.

## Next steps {#sec-next}

1. **Each school's own path**, relative to England, on the area pages and
   in [Find a twin](twins.qmd)'s fact cards.
2. **Illness or recording?** Started on [What goes with school
   absence](absence_causes.qmd#sec-recording), which finds a partial
   trade-off between illness and unauthorised absence.
3. **The severe tail**, which has tripled and is not falling, on its own.
4. **Trusts.** Whether particular trusts' schools move together after
   joining, which would point to what the trust does.
5. **Back into value added**: absence against intake, by kind, as a
   candidate for a future version of the model.

## The full results {#sec-full}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Within against between

```{r}
#| label: tbl-wb-full
#| tbl-cap: "Difference in each kind of absence (%) with the change shown, between schools (pooled with year effects) and within the same school (school and year fixed effects), 95% intervals clustered by school."
tibble::as_tibble(A$wb) |> mutate(o = factor(outcome, names(OUT))) |> arrange(o, desc(model), match(term, names(UNIT_LAB))) |>
  transmute(`Kind of absence` = OUT[outcome], Model = model, Change = UNIT_LAB[term],
            `%` = sgn(pct, 1), `95% interval` = sprintf("%+.1f to %+.1f", lo, hi)) |>
  kt(align = "lllrr") |> kableExtra::collapse_rows(columns = 1:2, valign = "top")
```

Without 2025/26, overall absence within a school rises
`r sgn(A$wb_check$pct[A$wb_check$outcome == "overall" & A$wb_check$term == "fsm"], 1)`%
with five points more FSM (against `r sgn(wbv("overall", "Within", "fsm"), 1)`%
with it), and unauthorised `r sgn(A$wb_check$pct[A$wb_check$outcome == "unauth" & A$wb_check$term == "fsm"], 1)`%
(against `r sgn(wbv("unauth", "Within", "fsm"), 1)`%).

### Who rose most

```{r}
#| label: tbl-shift-reg
#| tbl-cap: "The rise in each kind of absence from 2016/17–2018/19 to 2023/24–2025/26 (difference in log absence, as %) with one standard deviation more of each characteristic in 2018/19, with region effects; heteroskedasticity-robust 95% intervals."
tibble::as_tibble(A$shift$reg) |> mutate(o = factor(outcome, names(OUT)), p = pct(est), lo = pct(est - 1.96 * se), hi = pct(est + 1.96 * se)) |>
  arrange(o, match(term, names(X_LAB))) |>
  transmute(`Kind of absence` = OUT[outcome], Characteristic = A$x[term],
            `% per SD` = sgn(p, 1), `95% interval` = sprintf("%+.1f to %+.1f", lo, hi)) |>
  kt(align = "llrr") |> kableExtra::collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
```

### Event studies

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ev-full
#| tbl-cap: "Event-time estimates (% relative to the year before the change), all outcomes, with the number of changing schools observed at each event time."
tibble::as_tibble(EV) |> filter(rel >= -5, rel <= 5) |> mutate(o = factor(outcome, names(OUT))) |> arrange(study, o, rel) |>
  transmute(Study = study, `Kind of absence` = OUT[outcome], `Event time` = rel,
            `%` = sgn(pct, 1), `95% interval` = ifelse(rel == -1, "reference", sprintf("%+.1f to %+.1f", lo, hi)),
            Schools = schools) |>
  kt(align = "llrrrr") |> kableExtra::collapse_rows(columns = 1:2, valign = "top") |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "420px")
```

### Variance shares

```{r}
#| label: tbl-var
#| tbl-cap: "Share of the variation in log absence at each level, after national year effects, and the share of all variation that the year effects themselves account for."
A$var_dec |> select(outcome, level, share) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = share) |>
  mutate(o = factor(outcome, names(OUT))) |> arrange(o) |>
  transmute(`Kind of absence` = OUT[outcome],
            across(c(Region, `Local authority`, `School (lasting)`, `Year to year`), ~ paste0(round(100 * .x), "%")),
            `National year effects (of all)` = paste0(round(100 * A$year_share[outcome]), "%")) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrr")
```

:::

**Method.** Absence is modelled as log(% + 0.1), so effects read as %
differences. The variance shares come from `lme4` models with year fixed
effects and random intercepts for region, local authority and school. The
within and between models are `fixest` regressions of log absence on the
intake with school and year fixed effects (within) or year effects only
(between). The event studies use `fixest::sunab`, which estimates each
cohort's path separately and averages, avoiding the bias of a single
two-way fixed-effects estimate when changes are staggered; the reference is
the year before the change, and the comparison schools are those that did
not change in the period plus those yet to. A change is dated by the new
URN's opening date. Built by `R/09_absence_change.R`.
